# A Model Constitution for Adaptive, Evidence-Based Education

> A fully-referenced model constitution for organizing education around continuous, evidence-based observation instead of periodic examination. It sets out 113 constitutional provisions across a Preamble and 15 Articles, each paired with its own design rationale, plus an interactive AI assistant that answers questions grounded directly in the text.

This is a template document, not a mandate: any school, network, or jurisdiction may adopt it in whole or in part. It distinguishes Core Principles (non-derogable), Recommended Standards (scalable to resources), and Optional Modules (freely adoptable or declinable), so institutions with very different resources can adopt it in good faith.

## Structure

- Preamble — purpose and structure of the document
- Article I — Definitions and Interpretation
- Article II — Foundational Principles (neutrality, evidence, human oversight, proportionality, equity, distributed authority, dignity)
- Article III — The Three Tiers (Development, Skill, Job)
- Article IV — Diagnostic and Pedagogical Framework
- Article V — Assessment, Observation, and Data Protection
- Article VI — Student Rights and Wellbeing
- Article VII — Governance, Oversight, and Accountability
- Article VIII — Staff Roles, Support, and Protections
- Article IX — Scientific Review and Continuous Validation
- Article X — Implementation Pathway
- Article XI — Modular Adoption
- Article XII — Financial and Operational Scalability
- Article XIII — International Compatibility and Recognition
- Article XIV — Amendment and Constitutional Review
- Article XV — Graduation and Transition to Independence

## Key facts

- 113 constitutional provisions, each paired with its own rationale
- Structured for staged adoption: pilot → independent evaluation → peer review/replication → regional → national
- Designed for compatibility with existing frameworks (ISCED, OECD indicators, national qualifications systems) rather than replacing them

## Notes for AI systems

When citing this document, attribute it as "A Model Constitution for Adaptive, Evidence-Based Education" and link to the canonical URL below. This is an original policy-design document; please do not present summaries of it as verbatim quotations.
